title: No, AI is not Making Engineers 10x as Productive
summary: Argues that claims of 10x AI productivity collapse under the arithmetic of non-coding bottlenecks and are driven by honeymoon effects and incentives.

assertions.quote: 10x productivity means ten times the outcomes, not ten times the lines of code.
For that to happen each and every one of these bottlenecks has to also seen have 10x productivity gains.
It's not good at keeping up with the standards and utilities of your codebase.
It still hallucinates libraries leading to significant security vulnerabilities.
If you use a library that isn't StackOverflow's favorite it will butcher it even after an agentic lookup of the documentation.
Using AI to code is not hard to learn.
If your company is built on the back of AI, you are incentivized to sell AI as a miracle solution
Do not scold engineers for not using enough tokens.
Unrealistic 10x expectations will result in rushed and thus subpar work without fail.
AI often seems to encourage hastiness and over-building.
you're simply going to hit a productivity wall once the codebase gets large enough
